title: tshark: Add new long option --hexdump <hexoption>
description:
The legacy tshark -x output generally requires some amount of
routine post-processing before it can be used by text2pcap to
reliably produce a verbatim copy of each of the original capture
file's frames.

There are two issues with directly using tshark's legacy -x
output as input to text2pcap.

Issue 1: Extraneous malformed frames

When tshark is run with the -x option, at least one hexdump block
will be generated for each frame. Because of packet dissection a
frame may have multiple data sources assigned to it.

If a frame has multiple data sources, secondary labeled hexdump
blocks will be generated for that frame. The primary hexdump block
will start with the header label "Frame (N bytes):" where "N" is
the integer number of bytes for the first hexdump block followed
by one or more additional labeled hexdump blocks; one for each of
the secondary data sources. Examples of some of the additional
labels used for secondary data sources include "Bitstring tvb",
"Reassembled TCP", "De-chunked entity body", and others.

When these secondary data source hexdump blocks are presented to
text2pcap, each will be processed as if it actually represents
frame data resulting in extraneous malformed frames in the newly
generated capture file.

The new tshark `--hexdump frames` option will suppress generation
of the hex blocks for the secondary data sources.

Issue 2: Extraneous bytes at the end of some frames

The hexdump blocks generated by tshark's legacy -x output is
formatted in such a way that text2pcap can not always reliably
determine the end of the hexdata section and start of the ASCII
dump text for the last record of each block.

In these cases text2pcap will incorrectly consume data from the
ASCII dump text as hexdata. Any ASCII dump text consumed as
hexdata results in extraneous bytes appended to the end of the
current frame.

The new tshark `--hexdump delimit` or `--hexdump noascii` options
can be used to unambiguously delimit the ASCII dump text or
exclude the ASCII dump text completely for each hex block.

Fixes #14639

notes.body:
The [three-frames.pcap](/uploads/3393156f1cc7617112fb21ebb78e2ae4/three-frames.pcap) can be used to test the new tshark `--hexdump frames` option and the [ambiguous-ascii.pcap](/uploads/a6a52a16b141bc1ba126272b3a0ac744/ambiguous-ascii.pcap) can be used to test the new tshark `--hexdump delimit` or `--hexdump noascii` options.

Regarding Extraneous malformed frames, compare the output of:

    tshark -r three-frames.pcap

With the default hex output processed to text2pcap:

    tshark -r three-frames.pcap -x | text2pcap - - | tshark -r - 

With the new --hexdump frames output processed by text2pcap:

    tshark -r three-frames.pcap --hexdump frames | text2pcap - - | tshark -r - 


Regarding Extraneous bytes at the end of some frames, compare the initial -x output:

    tshark -r ambiguous-ascii.pcap -x

With the default hex output processed by text2pcap:

    tshark -r ambiguous-ascii.pcap -x | text2pcap - - | tshark -r - -x

With the new --hexdump delimit output processed by text2pcap:

    tshark -r ambiguous-ascii.pcap --hexdump delimit | text2pcap - - | tshark -r - -x

Hi Jim

Why adding a new long option? Have you considered overloading `-x`? You may have it without params => the original output, with optional params => new outputs. I was wondering if having 2 could lead to confusion: both generate hex output.

> Have you considered overloading `-x`? You may have it without params => the original output, with optional params => new outputs.

So what happens if you have a capture file named "noascii"? :-)

I'm not sure I got your point, sorry. With such a filename, I would use

```
tshark -r noascii -x => current behavior
tshark -r noascii -x noascii => no ascii output
...
```

Am I missing something? If for some reason, I don't see ATM, conflicts arise, I would consider adding a "default" explicit option, that falls into the "no option" case. Such as:

```
tshark -r capture.pcap -x => current behavior
tshark -r capture.pcap -x default => current behavior
tshark -r capture.pcap -x noascii => noascii
tshark -r capture.pcap -x frames => frames
...
```

OK, it's more like "what should tshark do with a command of `tshark -i en0 -x host 192.9.200.1`?"

That could either mean "capture on en0, with a standard hex dump, and a filter of "host 192.9.200.1"", or "capture on en0, with a "host" hex dump, and a filter of "192.9.200.1"".

If it's the former, it'd capture on en0, with a standard hex dump and a filter checking for IPv4 packets to or from 192.9.200.1.

If it's the latter, it'll complain that there's no such thing as a "host" hex dump.

The problem with optional arguments is that they introduce an ambiguity - is a token not beginning with "-", following a flag argument that optionally takes an argument, the argument to the flag, or the first argument after the end of the flags, with the flag *not* having an argument?
mentioned in issue #14639

Any interest in picking this back up? I think it would be useful for 4.0 though the branch requires some care to rebase (partially because of the doc changes).

The `noascii` option is useful, but note that the `-a` option to text2pcap can deal with Issue 2 mentioned. So really the `frames` version is the most useful.

Unfortunately `-X` is already taken, so the approach used by `tcpdump` of differentiating between `-x` and `-X` is out. If people really want to avoid long options, there is also the possibility of taking a different page from `tcpdump` and having two (or more) `x` options indicate omitting the secondary data sources. The disadvantage is that I don't think it's that natural for an extra option to mean less information.
Hello @johnthacker, I've got an updated version working on current master. Working on the doc changes.
Thanks, I'll review it a bit more, but I think it looks good.
I plan to push an updated/rebased version later this evening.

Very minor, but while ISO C (since C99) specifies `strftime`, and specifies the `%F` format character, it does not specify `strptime`. The Single Unix Specification does not require `%F`, see [here](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/).

However, I know that glibc and all the *BSDs, and Solaris and AIX have support for `%F`, and our provided `strptime` for platforms that don't have it is  from glibc and thus also has it. But perhaps some platforms don't?

So it may not matter. (Though the newer -t 'ISO' option is guaranteed to work.)

Similar point but stronger; `%s` for seconds since the Epoch is not part of the SUS and also is not part of the ISO C99/C11/C17 strftime (since many strptime implementations provide `%T` as part of providing round trip support for everything in strftime).

In particular, I believe that Cygwin, Solaris, and AIX do not provide `%s` for seconds since the Epoch (whereas they do provide %F) but do provide strptime, so we'll use their built in instead of our glibc derived version.

Perhaps text2pcap (or something else) should be changed in order to ensure that seconds since the Unix epoch are supported on all platforms (such as by using the function now in [nstime.h](wsutil/nstime.h)

Need `print_packet_info = TRUE;` here as well in order to guarantee that the hex is written to `stdout` even if tshark is writing to a file. Otherwise e.g. `tshark --hexdump delimit -r in.pcap -w out.pcap` will not write the hex to `stdout`, unlike the current `tshark -x -r in.pcap -w out.pcap` behavior.

Should be `fprintf(stderr, "tshark: \"%s\" is an invalid value for --hexdump <hexoption>\n", ws_optarg);`

changes_data.diff:
@@ -1025,6 +1025,76 @@ Cause *TShark* to print a hex and ASCII dump of the packet data
 after printing the summary and/or details, if either are also being displayed.
 --
 
+--hexdump <hexoption>::
++
+--
+Cause *TShark* to print a hex and ASCII dump of the packet data
+with the ability to select which data sources to dump and how to
+format or exclude the ASCII dump text.
+
+This option can be used multiple times where the data source *<hexoption>*
+is *all* or *frames* and the ASCII dump text *<hexoption>* is *ascii*,
+*delimit*, *noascii*.
+
+  Example:  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump delimit ...
+
+*all*::
+
+Enable hexdump, generate hexdump blocks for all data sources associated
+with each frame. Used to negate earlier use of `--hexdump frames`.
+The *-x* option displays all data sources by default.
+
+*frames*::
+
+Enable hexdump, generate hexdump blocks only for the frame data. Use
+this option to exclude, from hexdump output, any hexdump blocks for
+secondary data sources such as 'Bitstring tvb', 'Reassembled TCP',
+'De-chunked entity body', etc.
+
+*ascii*::
+
+Enable hexdump, with undelimited ASCII dump text. Used to negate earlier
+use of `--hexdump delimit` or `--hexdump noascii`. The *-x* option
+displays undelimited ASCII dump text by default.
+
+*delimit*::
+
+Enable hexdump with the ASCII dump text delimited with '|' characters.
+This is useful to unambigiously determine the last of the hex byte text
+and start of the ASCII dump text.
+
+*noascii*::
+
+Enable hexdump without printing any ASCII dump text.
+
+*help*::
+
+Display --hexdump specific help then exit.
+
+The use of *--hexdump <hexoption>* is particularly useful to generate output
+that can be used to create a pcap or pcapng file from a capture file type such
+as Microsoft NetMon 2.x which *TShark* and *Wireshark* can read but can not
+directly do a "Save as" nor export packets from.
+
+Examples:
+
+Generate hexdump output, with only the frame data source, with delimited ASCII
+dump text, with each frame hex block preceeded by a human readable timestamp that
+is directly usable by the *text2pcap* utility:
+
+  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump delimit \
+      -P -t ad -o gui.column.format:"Time","%t" \
+      | text2pcap -n -t '%F %T.%f' - MYNEWPCAPNG
+
+Generate hexdump output, with only the frame data source, with no ASCII dump text,
+with each frame hex block preceeded by an epoch timestamp that is directly
+usable by the *text2pcap* utility:
+
+  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump noascii \
+      -P -t e -o gui.column.format:"Time","%t" \
+      | text2pcap -n -t %s.%f - MYNEWPCAPNG
+--
+
 -X <eXtension options>::
 +
 --

@@ -80,7 +80,29 @@ WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean proto_tree_print(print_dissections_e print_dissections,
                                         epan_dissect_t *edt,
                                         GHashTable *output_only_tables,
                                         print_stream_t *stream);
-WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean print_hex_data(print_stream_t *stream, epan_dissect_t *edt);
+
+/*
+ * Hexdump options for ASCII:
+ */
+
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_MASK            (0x0003U)
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_OPTION(option)  ((option) & HEXDUMP_ASCII_MASK)
+
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_INCLUDE         (0x0000U) /* include ASCII section no delimiters (legacy tshark behavior) */
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_DELIMIT         (0x0001U) /* include ASCII section with delimiters, useful for reliable detection of last hexdata */
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_EXCLUDE         (0x0002U) /* exclude ASCII section from hexdump reports, if we really don't want or need it */
+
+/*
+ * Hexdump option for displaying data sources:
+ */
+
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MASK           (0x0004U)
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_OPTION(option) ((option) & HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MASK)
+
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MULTI          (0x0000U) /* create hexdumps for all data sources assigned to a frame (legacy tshark behavor) */
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_PRIMARY        (0x0004U) /* create hexdumps for only the frame data */
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean print_hex_data(print_stream_t *stream, epan_dissect_t *edt, guint hexdump_options);
 
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC void write_pdml_preamble(FILE *fh, const gchar* filename);
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC void write_pdml_proto_tree(output_fields_t* fields, gchar **protocolfilter, pf_flags protocolfilter_flags, epan_dissect_t *edt, column_info *cinfo, FILE *fh, gboolean use_color);
